findings.issue: `paired_outcome_vs_sven` inverts the `a_better` count for `final_test_acc`. It reuses paired.py's loss convention (`a_better = (d < 0).sum()`, documented there as "a < b means A is better FOR A LOSS") on a metric where larger is better, so every accuracy row claims the opposite of what happened. Recomputed from experiment_results/cifar10_resnet_ce_scan_confirm: Sven test acc 0.52976 vs Muon 0.77930, paired mean -0.2495 on 5/5 seeds -- Sven loses on all five -- yet analysis/tables/paired_final_test_acc_cifar10_resnet_ce_scan.md prints `a_better = 5` for Muon (the `final_test_loss` twin correctly prints 0). All four exported accuracy tables are affected (mnist_scan_ce, mnist_scan_labelRegression, both CIFAR), and the `sort_values('mean')` puts the rows where Sven is furthest BEHIND at the top with no sign note, which reads as the opposite of the loss tables directly above them. `ranking_summary`'s rank_acc is correct (ascending=False), so only this table is wrong.
findings.suggested_fix: Flip the count when the metric is an accuracy: `better = int((d > 0).sum()) if style.higher_is_better(metric) else int((d < 0).sum())`, or negate `d` for accuracy metrics and say so in `tbl.attrs['sign']`; rename the column to `sven_better` and state the convention in the notebook cell 11 title. Add a unit test that pins the accuracy sign (the current fixture only exercises `final_test_loss`, whose curve is 1.1x val, so the bug cannot be caught).

findings.issue: The cross-scan table titled "Selection optimism: (confirmation - tuning) / tuning" (notebook cell 8, exported as analysis/tables/selection_optimism.md) and the report's "gap" column use the POOLED gap for toy/polynomial, which compares 15 confirmation runs on 3 data seeds against 5 tuning runs on 1 data seed. Almost all of it is problem-instance variation, not selection optimism, and for toy it has the wrong sign. Recomputed: polynomial median pooled gap +22.59% with "15/15 methods worse on confirm", but on the tuning instance (data_seed 2000) the median gap is -1.75% and only 7/15 are worse; Sven +26.8% pooled vs +0.64% same-instance. Toy Sven +77.05% pooled vs -63.4% same-instance (val_tune 2.873e-07 -> val_conf_ds0 1.051e-07). Cell 26 then concludes "The selection optimism is small but real", which for these two scans is a statement about data_seed 1001/2001 being harder problems. The module already computes `gap_val_same_instance` and the per-scan tables show `val, tuning instance`, so the right number exists but is not the one summarised.
findings.suggested_fix: In cell 8 report `gap_val_same_instance / val_tune` as the selection-optimism column for every scan (it equals `gap_val_rel` where there are no data seeds) and put the pooled gap in a second column labelled as including the two unseen problem instances; fix the cell-26 sentence. Same for the "gap"/"gap rel" columns of `confirmation_view` on toy/polynomial, and for the report's summary table.

findings.issue: Cell 26's conclusion states CIFAR-CE "last on test accuracy (53.0% against 68-78%)". Recomputed from the confirmation records, the ten baselines span 56.77% (SGDm) to 77.93% (Muon): SGDm 0.56774 and PolyakSGD 0.63158 both fall below 68%. Sven being last (rank 11/11) is correct, but the quoted range describes only 8 of the 10 baselines. (The plan's decision 3 says "73-78%", also wrong; the implementer's report flagged two other decision-3 corrections but not this one.)
findings.suggested_fix: Write "53.0% against 56.8-77.9% (73-78% for the eight strongest baselines)" and add the corrected range to the report's decision-3 corrections list so WP4b/WP5 and the paper text pick it up.

findings.issue: The report claims `timing_join_report` "reproduces [bench/check_timing_join.py]'s deviation check". It does not: the loop only compares runs whose `final_val_loss` is finite, and add_derived NaNs a diverged run, so a standalone twin that diverged is dropped from the deviation statistics. I ran bench/check_timing_join.py independently: its worst finding on mnist_scan_labelRegression is `std_bs64_mlp_width32_lr0.01_optimSOAP_mseed3001_lseed3000`, final val 0.90099645 (scan) vs 184.84679 (timing) = 204x; headline's table for that scan reports SOAP `max_rel_dev = 0.2058, n_joined = 4` and never surfaces the 204x. Separately, the printed table contradicts the docstring's own expectation ("Sven and the plain first-order MLP runs are expected not to [deviate]", plan section 0): Sven is `bit_reproduced = False` on mnist_scan_labelRegression (1.26e-3) and mnist_scan_ce (3.80e-2) while SGD/SGDm/RMSprop are ~1e-7 there. Neither the notebook nor the report flags that.
findings.suggested_fix: Count a timing run whose scan twin finished but which itself diverged (or vice versa) as its own column, e.g. `n_diverged_only_in_timing`, and assert/print it; drop or qualify the "reproduces check_timing_join" claim. Add a note where Sven's MNIST deviation is printed -- either the plan's reproducibility fact needs correcting or the MNIST timing pass needs explaining (Sven's rtol truncation rank is data-dependent, so a 1e-7 kernel difference can flip a kept singular value).

findings.issue: `scan_inflation` is documented and narrated as contention cost only: `run_efficiency`'s docstring says a scan wall time "is inflated by the other shards on the same GPU", `efficiency_table`'s says "inflated by shard contention", and cell 26 concludes "`scan_inflation` is what sharding cost, not a property of any optimizer". The records say otherwise for the MLP scans: every record I sampled has `n_shards = 1`, and toy_1d_scan / mnist_scan_* ran overwhelmingly on `NVIDIA A100-SXM4-40GB MIG 3g.20gb` (357/400, 392/400, 369/400) while all 425 timing runs ran on a full `NVIDIA A100-SXM4-80GB`. So the 2.6-3.1x MLP inflation mixes co-tenancy (I measured up to 14 concurrent runs in one mnist_scan_labelRegression job) with a GPU-capability change, and is not a clean "what sharding cost" number. CIFAR and nanoGPT scans did run on A100-80GB, so their inflation (1.05-3.6x) is the contention part alone.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the GPU type per pass to the efficiency table (e.g. modal `gpu_name` for the scan rows and the timing rows) and reword both docstrings and cell 26 to "co-tenancy plus, on the MLP scans, a MIG 3g.20gb slice against a full A100-80GB".

findings.issue: Every CIFAR-CE row is provisional and nothing says so. The decision-5 rtol extension is running right now: `squeue` shows five `p2_cifar_ce_rtol` jobs, and `tools/reconcile.py --all` reports cifar10_resnet_ce_scan expected 785 / on disk 745 with 5 claimed-live and 35 never-started (the `mode=svd k_values=[128] lrs=[0.05,0.1,0.5] rtol=[0.03,0.1,0.3]` override group; 5 of its 45 runs have landed). The selection of record was written 2026-09-20T03:58, before those runs, and decision 5 says select_best must be re-run afterwards, so the selected Sven config, its 9/11 rank and the CIFAR-CE efficiency row can all move. The notebook's only visible hint is `cifar10_resnet_ce_scan ... 100 missing` in cell 3 -- but that 100 is HIG (parked, also 100 on cifar10_resnet_scan_labelRegression, which reconcile calls complete), a different thing, so a reader is more likely to be misled than warned. The `[config_table] 9 configuration(s) with no result file at all (45 runs)` line buried in cell 15's output is the real signal.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a cell that prints, per scan, the selection file's `generated_at` against the newest record mtime in the scan directory and the reconcile never-started/claimed-live counts, and fails loudly (or prints a PROVISIONAL banner) when a scan has in-flight runs. State in the report that the CIFAR-CE table must be regenerated after the rtol extension lands.

findings.issue: `time_to_target_table`'s `n_never` merges two different facts: runs that trained to the end and never reached the target, and runs that diverged (`epochs_to_target` returns None for them at line 1113). The exported table has `n_runs`, `n_reached`, `n_never` and no divergence column, so analysis/tables/time_to_target_polynomial_scan.md reads "Stochastic L-BFGS, n_runs 15, n_reached 0, n_never 15" when 13 of those 15 diverged and only 2 ever ran to completion. Same for toy L-BFGS (n_never 13 of which 1 diverged) and for the ineligible rows generally. A second, smaller point: on toy/polynomial the pre-declared targets are single pooled values applied across three different random problems, so an `epochs` mean can be conditional on which instance a run was on (polynomial's hard target 0.1086 is unreachable on instance 2001), which the docstring does not mention.
findings.suggested_fix: Split `n_never` into `n_never_reached` and `n_diverged` (and carry `elig_conf` into the row), and note the per-instance caveat in the docstring or declare the toy/polynomial targets per data seed.

findings.issue: `_stats` returns std 0.0 for n = 1, which propagates into `val_conf_seedspread` and is then printed as a real spread: analysis/tables/confirmation_polynomial_scan.md shows Stochastic L-BFGS with `val, within-instance seed std = 0` because each surviving data seed contributed exactly one run. A reader sees perfect seed reproducibility where there is one sample.
findings.suggested_fix: Return NaN for n = 1 (and let `fmt_pm` print the bare mean), or blank `val_conf_seedspread` when every per-instance n is 1.

findings.issue: `run_efficiency`'s docstring calls `sync_train_s` "the sum of ``train_times``, i.e. SYNCHRONISED per-batch training time". The records store one `train_times` entry per EPOCH (len == num_epochs == 20/50, and mean(train_times) == avg_train_time, e.g. 62.219 s for CIFAR-CE Sven); per-batch time is the separate `avg_batch_time_train` key. The arithmetic (`ms_per_step = 1e3 * sum / steps`) is correct and I reproduced 177.3 ms/step for CIFAR-CE Sven and 20.86 for nanoGPT, so only the wording misleads.
findings.suggested_fix: Say "the sum of the per-epoch synchronised training times" and note that `avg_batch_time_train` is the per-batch figure.

findings.issue: Two small hygiene items. (a) `headline.epochs_to_target` shadows `analysis_helpers.epochs_to_target` (line 271 there) with different semantics -- None vs NaN, plus a diverged guard -- and both are importable into the same notebook namespace. (b) `write_table`'s LaTeX output embeds the raw U+00B1 from `fmt_pm` (see analysis/tables/confirmation_cifar10_resnet_ce_scan.tex) and the docstring mentions only the booktabs requirement.
findings.suggested_fix: Rename to `headline.epochs_to_target_strict` (or take the diverged guard as a keyword on the shared helper), and either emit `$\pm$` in the LaTeX path or document the utf8 inputenc requirement alongside booktabs.
